title: Tissue Procurement: Biosafety Guidelines
author: Kerry Wiles
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6y6hfze
materials: Storage and disposal of all collection materials, including laboratory samples upon aliquot completion must be done in compliance with Biosafety levels of materials. Proper and recognized safe procedures for disposal of blood products or other contaminated materials include Autoclaving for 1 hour at 121 degree Celsius or incineration. Biohazardous trash will be picked up when needed by the Lab Techs, but you may call them to schedule the pick up.

steps.title: Prepare Personal Protective Equipment
steps.instruction: Don appropriate personal protective gear, including eyeglasses, face shields, lab coats, and gloves.

substeps.instruction: Determine if double-gloving is necessary based on specimen size (e.g., breast) to allow for quick removal of contaminated gloves.
Keep a spare set of gloves nearby to avoid reaching across the lab bench and contaminating clothing.

steps.title: Prepare Collection Containers
steps.instruction: Prepare an appropriate number of clearly labeled containers placed in an ice bucket, categorized by tissue type and anatomic site.

substeps.instruction: Ensure each anatomic site and tissue type has its own separate container.
Ensure normal and tumor tissues are never placed in contact with each other.

steps.title: Transport and Receive Tissue
steps.instruction: Transport tissue from the OR to surgical pathology as quickly and safely as possible.

substeps.instruction: Transport tissue on ice and ensure it is covered.

steps.title: Section Tissue
steps.instruction: Section tissue using clean surfaces and separate instruments to prevent cross-contamination.

substeps.instruction: Use only clean wax paper or the back of blue Chux for cutting.
Avoid absorbent materials to prevent capillary action from drawing tissue fluid or lymph nodes out of the tissue.
Use different scalpels and cutting surfaces for different tissues from the same patient (e.g., liver vs. colon) and for different tissue types (e.g., tumor vs. normal).

steps.title: Manage Glove Contamination
steps.instruction: Change gloves frequently to avoid contaminating lab areas using a specific removal technique to keep bloody areas inside the glove.

substeps.instruction: Gently grab the area near the base of the thumb of one hand and pull up and over the fingers to partially remove the glove.
Insert a clean-gloved finger under the top of the other glove near the wrist and pull it over the hand.
If double-gloved, use the inside of the first removed glove to pull off the second glove.

steps.title: Clean and Dispose of Materials
steps.instruction: Thoroughly clean the procurement area after each donor and dispose of instruments correctly.

substeps.instruction: Place procurement instruments in the 'dirty' bin for retrieval, cleaning, and sterilization.
